selection_rule: candidate decisions use repeated-census structure, stable unit identity, geometry, survey design, data accessibility and prior Structural provenance; no candidate is promoted because a source-leverage effect direction is known

candidates.system: Azores BALA repeated native-forest arthropod surveys

metadata.core_sites_reported: 30 in description; 31 in one Project Data sentence; raw Event audit required
metadata.phase_prose: BALA1, BALA2, BALA3 with internally inconsistent date ranges requiring raw Event resolution

candidates.decision_reason: BALA is the closest structural match to the v1.123 three-time hypothesis because the same core sites were deliberately resampled in three major phases under a common protocol. It is not confirmatory-eligible until raw Event rows resolve the 30-versus-31 core-site and phase-date discrepancies, a stable repeated panel is frozen, and a deterministic taxon-level pilot/confirmatory split is created without semantic confirmatory occurrence access.

candidates.system: Azores long-term forest arthropod SLAM monitoring

metadata.occurrence_extension_records_reported: 14922 in Data Records section versus 14924 in methods text; raw archive must resolve
metadata.sampling_frequency: approximately four standardized SLAM-trap collections per year
metadata.critical_taxonomic_gap: Pico and Terceira Araneae are intentionally excluded from the main archive and published separately

candidates.decision_reason: Event/occurrence separation permits a clean effort audit before taxon outcomes. It remains a strong backup candidate, but BALA now ranks ahead because BALA has an explicit repeated three-wave core panel rather than requiring three-time windows to be constructed from annual coverage.

candidates.system: Finnish Archipelago Bird Census / Common Eider (Somateria mollissima)

metadata.standard_monitoring: breeding numbers estimated by at least two annual counts under Archipelago Bird Census guidelines for the core monitoring programme
metadata.known_data_complication: some grouped-island counts were redistributed to individual islands; publication reports about 6.2% of observations per year affected

candidates.decision_reason: Strong independent retrospective stress-test geometry, but broad response direction is already published and some island counts were reconstructed from grouped reports. It cannot count as pristine confirmation.
Long-term repeated island monitoring exists, but the required raw annual island-by-species sequence with a frozen survey-effort rule has not been located.

candidates.system: Thousand Island Lake long-term vegetation plots
candidates.decision_reason: A same-protocol three-census island-by-species matrix has not yet been established from the located public material.
The archived derivative does not document the complete-checklist and effort fields needed to distinguish surveyed zero from non-reporting for a focal species.
A-Islands is already a Structural discovery system for source-network hypotheses and cannot independently confirm this mechanism.

preferred_response_unopened_preintake.reason: BALA supplies an explicit three-wave repeated core-site panel under a common protocol, matching t0 source state, t1 source loss and t2 downstream contraction without selecting calendar windows from outcomes.
